Comparing FY2024 net income across the five carriers:

- Delta Air Lines: $3,457M net income [DOC-1]
- United Airlines Holdings: $3,149M net income [DOC-1]
- American Airlines Group: $846M net income [DOC-1]
- Alaska Air Group: $395M net income [DOC-1]
- Southwest Airlines: $465M net income [DOC-1]

Note on comparability: Alaska Air Group's FY2024 results are not fully comparable to the other four companies' full-year, standalone results because Alaska completed its acquisition of Hawaiian Holdings on September 18, 2024, and Hawaiian's results (which included a $113 million net loss on $869 million of revenue) are only consolidated into Alaska's financials from that date forward, not for the full year [DOC-2]. This partial-period consolidation means Alaska's reported net income reflects a mix of a full year of legacy Alaska operations plus roughly 3.5 months of Hawaiian, whereas Delta, United, American, and Southwest each report on a full-year, single-entity basis for the entire period [DOC-1][DOC-2]. This does not change the overall ranking, however, since Alaska's net income is the lowest of the five regardless.

Based on net income, Delta Air Lines was the most profitable of the five airlines in fiscal year 2024, with net income of $3,457 million, exceeding United ($3,149M), American ($846M), Southwest ($465M), and Alaska ($395M) [DOC-1]. Delta also had the highest operating income ($5,995M) among the group [DOC-1].

ANSWER: Delta Air Lines was the most profitable in FY2024, with net income of $3,457 million (and operating income of $5,995 million), the highest among Delta, United, Southwest, American, and Alaska.
